question: How many tonnes of coal per hour does 40% NH3 blending save compared with pure coal firing?
rendered:
According to the text on page 3, the total coal feed rate is 166.14 t·h^−1. 

On page 7, the coal feeding rate under pure coal firing and 40% NH3 blending are given as 30.5 kg·s^−1 and 30.5 kg·s^−1 respectively. 

To convert this to tonnes per hour, we multiply by 3600 (to convert seconds to hours) and divide by 1000 (to convert kg to t):

(30.5 kg·s^−1 * 3600 s·h^−1) / 1000 kg·t^−1 = 109.8 t·h^−1 

The coal feeding rate under pure coal firing is given as 50.83 kg·s^−1, which is 183 t·h^−1 (as given on page 3). 

The difference in coal feeding rate between pure coal firing and 40% NH3 blending is therefore 183 t·h^−1 - 109.8 t·h^−1 = 73.2 t·h^−1 

Therefore, 40% NH3 blending saves 73.2 tonnes of coal per hour compared with pure coal firing.
